transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Chris Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Sofia Ramos, Ethan Cole, Priya Desai (Nimbus Analytics)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, brief):
- Quick sync on SDK integration, function/tool-calling checkpoints, and structured-output contract.
- Discussed intermittent JSON parse errors and mismatch in schema for 'customer_profile' object.
- Agreed next steps: SDK snippet update, targeted test runs, and VPC egress validation; pricing follow-up for Dedicated pilot.

Topics: SDK integration, function-calling behavior, structured-output schema, KV cache/latency tradeoffs, VPC networking for Private test, benchmark artifacts.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick roll call — Jordan from Redwood here, Maya SE, Chris CSM — and who do we have on the Nimbus side?
[00:12] Sofia Ramos: Hi this is Sofia, thanks. Ethan and Priya are on as well.
[00:17] Ethan Cole: Yeah hi, thanks.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Cool. Agenda — 1) SDK integration bits and a small code snippet issue, 2) function-calling edge cases we saw yesterday, 3) structured output mismatch and parsing errors, quick network note for private deployment.

[00:34] Maya Patel: I'll start with the SDK item — thanks. So last week we pushed v1.4.3 of the client lib to your test env, and the main change was the structured_output field now supports both "schema_v1" and "schema_v2". We noticed one of the runs from your infra threw a parsing exception when the model returned an array where we expected an object, so I dug into the call.
[01:02] Priya Desai: Yeah that was the one — it failed in about 8% of attempts on the QA prompts, and it bubbled up to our downstream parser which is strict JSON.
[01:13] Maya Patel: Right. There's a couple causes — sometimes the model picks a compact enum style and returns ["value"] and sometimes it returns {"value": true}. We're recommending the SDK do a lightweight normalization step and then validate against the schema. We can share snippet.
[01:34] Sofia Ramos: That would help. Our pipeline is in Go and it's brittle about unexpected arrays.

[02:00] Jordan Lee: On the pricing / capacity side, quick note — Nimbus is in the stage where you might compare Hosted vs Dedicated. We'll send a compact delta with p50/p95 latency and cost per 1M tokens so you can do rough math.
[02:18] Ethan Cole: For Dedicated we need to understand autoscale behaviour — like can it burst for overnight jobs? The pilot needs predictable throughput but sometimes batch jobs spike.
[02:30] Chris Alvarez: Yes, Dedicated supports burst pools; we'll include recommended config for autoscaling and safe burst headroom.

[03:00] Maya Patel: Back to function-calling — we reproduced the case where the function name is present but the args don't match the declared param types, which caused the client to throw. In your test run the model returned function_call: { name: "update_profile", arguments: "{\"id\": 123, \"attrs\": [\"x\"]}" } but the schema expected attrs to be object not array.
[03:34] Sofia Ramos: Right, we saw that. It looks like the KV cache hit occasionally returns a different shape when the prompt includes a short context.
[03:45] Maya Patel: It's likely model variance + prompt primer. Two mitigations: 1) server-side normalization in SDK, 2) instructive prompt to force object shape — e.g., include an example in the system prompt.
[04:05] Jordan Lee: Do you have their sample prompts handy, Sofia?
[04:10] Sofia Ramos: Yes I'll push the prompt set to the shared drive after the call.

[05:00] Ethan Cole: Another question — latency. In our staging runs the p95 jumped from 220ms to 480ms when we enabled the K V cache and batching. That seems counterintuitive.
[05:18] Maya Patel: Hmm, K V cache (sometimes transcribed as K V) can add a slight prefetch overhead when it's cold. Also batching introduces queuing for throughput; if your request pattern is spiky, batching might increase tail latency unless you tune max_batch_delay_ms or use lower batch size for low concurrency routes.
[05:50] Jordan Lee: We should dig into per-token breakdowns — Maya, can you provide token-level timing and where the latency spikes occur?
[05:58] Maya Patel: Yep, I'll paste a mini flamegraph. Also, make sure you're using the pinned model variant; we saw that an unpinned latest can shift behavior.

[06:30] Priya Desai: For structured output — our parser expects the top-level object to contain "customer_profile" with keys id, name, attrs. But the model sometimes nests attrs under "properties". Is there an easy mapping?
[06:50] Maya Patel: Two options: SDK mapping layer (we can add a compatibility shim) or change prompt to enforce the key name. For speed I'd suggest mapping shim in SDK for the pilot.
[07:10] Jordan Lee: We're going to prototype a mapping shim and share it as a small patch in the repo.

[07:30] Sofia Ramos: Sounds good. Also, small security question — we're planning a Private test inside our VPC next week. What about egress rules and your side's control plane?
[07:46] Chris Alvarez: For Private we require a connector that terminates inside your VPC and uses outbound-only egress to Redwood endpoints. We'll share an egress checklist — ports, CIDR, and names of endpoints. Also note that if you want on-prem air-gapped, that's a separate package.
[08:10] Ethan Cole: The checklist will be useful. We need to validate with our infra team.

[09:00] Jordan Lee: Quick demo segment — Maya, maybe show the updated SDK snippet and the schema validator?
[09:08] Maya Patel: Sure. I'm going to paste — (inaudible typing) — OK, snippet does lightweight normalization: if field is array and schema expects object, convert first element to key: true pattern then validate. I know it's imperfect but avoids the downstream crash.
[09:40] Sofia Ramos: Can you drop that in the shared drive?
[09:44] Maya Patel: Yep, will do.

[10:10] Jordan Lee: Let's talk about logs. Sofia mentioned the parse exceptions — do you get the raw model output in your logs?
[10:18] Sofia Ramos: We do, but the names are messy and sometimes the function call object is flattened by our ingestion.
[10:25] Maya Patel: We recommend enabling structured logging at the SDK layer and also keep raw_response for debugging. We can add a toggle to redact user PII.

[12:00] Priya Desai: Another small item — function-calling with tool invocation: we tried hooking a downstream microservice and got a 502 intermittently, unclear whether it's the tool or the SDK retry logic.
[12:18] Maya Patel: 502 suggests the tool endpoint returned error; SDK will retry on 5xx with exponential backoff by default, but you can adjust retry policy. We'll want the tool logs and the SDK debug logs.
[12:34] Ethan Cole: We'll capture and share the service logs.

[13:00] Jordan Lee: On quality/regression monitoring — we pointed you at Redwood Optimize for prompt set evaluation. Did you have a chance to run the synthetic suite?
[13:10] Sofia Ramos: We ran a small set; results were ok but the scoring threshold needs to be tuned. We'll upload the results sheet.
[13:20] Chris Alvarez: We'll review and suggest threshold adjustments. Also, we'll add an alert when quality dips more than X% compared to baseline.

[15:00] Maya Patel: Quick note on model variants — you were using rwin-13b-int8 for some tests; there's a newer rwin-13b-q4 that changes output spacing slightly and might affect strict parsers. Recommend freezing the variant for the pilot.
[15:22] Sofia Ramos: OK we'll pin that.

[16:00] Jordan Lee: Anything on security/compliance? Priya?
[16:05] Priya Desai: We need SOC 2 artifacts and an architecture diagram for the Private deployment. Any chance you can share redacted diagrams?
[16:15] Chris Alvarez: Yes, we'll send SOC2 summary, and an infra diagram with call flow. Expect both by 2026-03-22.

[18:00] Ethan Cole: One more operational quirk — connector missed heartbeats for about 3 mins yesterday during our smoke tests. Not sure if that's your side or our network flapping.
[18:16] Maya Patel: We'll check connector metrics — heartbeat, reconnect rate. Also check NAT gateway timeouts on your side.

[20:00] Jordan Lee: Let's set the near-term plan — Maya will produce SDK snippet and mapping shim; Sofia/Ethan will run the structured-output QA with new snippet; Jordan will send pricing delta and Dedicated config; Chris will send SOC2 + infra diagram + egress checklist.

[21:00] Sofia Ramos: Sounds good. One ask — can we get a smaller reproducible test that fails fast so our CI can catch it?
[21:12] Maya Patel: Yep, we'll add a short failing-case set (10 prompts) that cause the parse error and integrate into your CI.

[22:00] Priya Desai: Timeline check — we want to run the Private test by 2026-03-30, so the SDK and network checklist need to land this week.
[22:10] Jordan Lee: That aligns — we'll aim to hit those dates.

[24:00] (brief silence / typing)

[25:00] Transcript noise: brief crosstalk between Sofia and Ethan about internal tickets.

[26:00] Jordan Lee: Any blockers from Nimbus side?
[26:05] Sofia Ramos: Main blocker is infra time this week but we'll prioritize.

[28:00] Maya Patel: Quick technical aside — when you run the function-calling path, enable the verbose schema check in the SDK; it adds 10-20ms but it's worth it during testing.
[28:20] Ethan Cole: Okay, we can enable it in staging.

[30:00] Jordan Lee: Let's capture explicit next steps before we close.
[30:10] Chris Alvarez: I'll summarize and post in the CRM thread.

[31:00] Rapid recap:
- Maya: SDK mapping shim + structured-output examples + failing-case set (due 2026-03-23)
- Jordan: Pricing delta + Dedicated autoscale config (due 2026-03-22)
- Chris: SOC2 summary, infra diagram, egress checklist (due 2026-03-22)
- Sofia/Ethan: Run QA with updated SDK, share logs (due 2026-03-24)

[33:00] Sofia Ramos: Thanks, will do.

[34:00] (small discussion about who will demo the failing case in the next call)

[36:00] Jordan Lee: Proposed follow-up meeting — 2026-03-25 same time to validate Private test readiness and early results. Does that work?
[36:10] Sofia Ramos: Works for us.

[38:00] Priya Desai: Also please include any guidance for content redaction — our legal wants to know how logs are redacted.
[38:12] Chris Alvarez: We'll include the log-redaction guide in the SOC2 packet.

[40:00] Maya Patel: Small gotcha I noticed — when the model calls a tool with nested arguments, the SDK's current JSON flattening loses order info; not critical now but may surface for a mapping shim. We'll note it in the patch.

[42:00] Jordan Lee: Alright thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the thread.

Action items (as recorded in call):
- Maya Patel | Create mapping shim + add 10 failing prompts | due 2026-03-23
- Jordan Lee | Send pricing delta and Dedicated config | due 2026-03-22

End of transcript.
